cards.front: Recall a key point about Selecting and Working with Materials
cards.back: Timber working: tenon saw (straight cuts), coping saw (curves), chisel (paring and mortising), plane (flat surfaces), file/sandpaper (smooth finish). Jointing: PVA glue, screws, dowels, dovetails, mortise-and-tenon.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selecting and Working with Materials
cards.back: Metal working: hacksaw (cutting bar/flat stock), pillar drill (accurate holes), file (shaping and deburring), sheet metal snips (cutting thin sheet), tap and die (internal/external threads). Joining: soldering, brazing, welding, rivets, nuts and bolts.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selecting and Working with Materials
cards.back: Polymer working: laser cutter (2D profiles from sheet acrylic/MDF), line bender (folds acrylic along a heated element), strip heater, drill (slow speed to avoid melting). Joining: acrylic cement (capillary action), solvent weld (PVC), ultrasonic welding, snap-fit joints.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selecting and Working with Materials
cards.back: Workshop safety: tie hair back, no loose clothing, safety goggles for all cutting/drilling, clamp work in a vice, use push sticks on machinery, know emergency stop positions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Selecting and Working with Materials
cards.back: Material preparation: measure twice cut once, mark out with scribe (metal) or pencil/marking gauge (timber), allow for material removed by the saw blade (kerf), file edges to remove burrs.

cards.front: What should you know about d&t exam tips?
cards.back: For practical process questions: 1) Name the tool/process, 2) Describe the steps in order, 3) State safety precautions, 4) Name the material it is suitable for, 5) Explain why this process is appropriate.

cards.front: What does PVA wood glue mean?

cards.back: Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A laser cutter can cut through any material including thick metal. Correct: Laser cutters used in schools typically have 40-60 W CO2 tubes that can cut: acrylic (up to approx 10 mm), MDF/plywood (up to approx 6 mm), card, paper, fabric. They CANNOT cut: metals (CO2 laser wavelength reflects off metal surfaces), PVC (releases toxic chlorine gas), polycarbon

You need to make a 3 mm acrylic display stand. Describe the complete making process from sheet material to finished product, including cutting, bending, joining and finishing, with appropriate safety precautions.

AQA D&T 8552: Written exam 50% + NEA 50%. AOs: AO1 Recall (20%), AO2 Apply (30%), AO3 Analyse & evaluate (50%). For grade 9, demonstrate detailed practical knowledge of making processes and precise step-by-step descriptions with safety awareness.
